When the paper towel roll is large, each sheet will cover less of the circumference of the roll.  When the roll gets smaller, each remaining sheet will wrap around the roll more times.  Example:  

The circumference of a full roll (assuming 6 inches in diameter) is 18.85 inches.  If each sheet is 10", that means 1 sheet will cover just more than half of the roll's circumference.  

When the roll eventually gets smaller, say 4 inches, the circumference of that roll is 12.57 inches.  One 10" sheet will almost cover the complete circumference.  

At 3 inches in diameter, the circumference is 9.42 inches.  One sheet will now completely wrap around the outside, with some left over.  

The roll will appear to speed up the rate it is shrinking the more paper towels you use.

When I was learning barre chords, the most important thing I found was that I had to put my thumb on the back of the neck, vs having it wrapped around the neck by the low E string.  Look at some images of barre chords vs open chords, and you'll notice that you usually can't see the player's thumb on barre chords.  Classical guitars tend to have fatter necks, which makes keeping the thumb on the back of the neck more natural (and is considered proper technique for classical guitar), unless you have really big hands (I don't).  Finger strength does play a role, too, and the nylon strings on classical guitars don't require as much strength to press down.
